about: Drum and band patterns from the DJOPS genre guide, two bars of 16 steps. Written by tools/export_genre_player.py; do not edit by hand.

downtempo.name: Downtempo
downtempo.hint: Broken kick that never lands on every beat, soft snare, a swung shaker, a warm bass and a pad underneath.

downtempo_b.name: Downtempo · trip-hop feel
downtempo_b.hint: A heavier swung beat with a full snare on 2 and 4 — still no kick on every beat.

psychill.name: Psychill (Downtempo)
psychill.hint: No driving kick: a loose beat, a soft bass, long pads and a slow acid line drifting on top.

downtempo_c.name: Downtempo · Andean / cumbia organica, 96
downtempo_c.hint: No house kick: a soft kick on 1 and 3, a cumbia shaker pushing the off-beats, a hand drum answering, and a flute over a warm bass.

organic.name: Organic House
organic.hint: A soft straight kick, a quiet 16th shaker bed, hand drums answering between the beats, a round bass and a flute over a warm pad. No drum sticks out.

organic_b.name: Organic House · slow house, 108
organic_b.hint: House rule 3: a straight kick at 100-112 is still Organic House. Shaker, conga and a flute line over it.

afro.name: Afro House
afro.hint: Straight kick under DENSE percussion: shakers on every 16th and congas falling between the beats.

afro_b.name: Afro House · afro tech, 124
afro_b.hint: Tighter and darker: dense percussion still drives it, with a short synth bass instead of a pad.

afro_c.name: Afro House · 3Step, 118
afro_c.hint: Three kicks, then a gap on beat 4 that pulls you into the next bar. Shakers and woodblocks keep running, and a log drum plays the bass.

deep.name: Deep House
deep.hint: A soft kick on every beat, a swung 16th shaker, jazzy chord stabs leading and a muted, warm bass.

deep_b.name: Deep House · dubby
deep_b.hint: The soft-kick side of dub techno: one echoing chord stab, a soft kick, a held bass. At 124 or less with a soft kick it stays in Deep House, where slow dub-tinged deep house sits; a techno kick moves it to Techno.

house.name: House · classic piano house
house.hint: A drum-machine kick on every beat, clap on 2 and 4, an open hat on the off-beat, and a bright piano stab with a plain, bouncing bass. The stab leads; the bass only supports.

house_b.name: House · jackin, 126
house_b.hint: The same kick and clap with a strong swing: shuffled 16th hats, short stabs that jump off the beat and a bouncing bass between the kicks. The swing is the Jackin tag.

minimal.name: Minimal / Deep Tech
minimal.hint: A soft straight kick, shuffled hats, tiny clicks, and a short, bouncy off-beat bass. Very little else.

minimal_b.name: Minimal / Deep Tech · skippy, 128
minimal_b.hint: Clicks just after each kick and a bass that skips around the beat.

minimal_c.name: Minimal / Deep Tech · deep tech bounce, 128
minimal_c.hint: Still small and dry, but the bass rolls in short 16ths between the kicks and a crisp 16th hat runs on top. No drop: it just keeps bouncing.

tech.name: Tech House
tech.hint: Punchy kick on every beat, clap on 2 and 4, open hats on the off-beat, and a rubbery bass hook that is the star.

tech_b.name: Tech House · rolling bass, 124
tech_b.hint: The bass rolls in pairs between the kicks, with a vocal-chop stab: the groove is the whole track.

melodic.name: Melodic House · vocal-led, 122 (sketch)
melodic.hint: A warm kick on every beat, a clap on 2 and 4, an off-beat hat and a rolling bass. A vocal leads over a soft pad (a lead synth sings its line here): the vocal decides, whether the track stays level or builds.

prog.name: Progressive House
prog.hint: A rolling straight kick, a bass that rolls two notes into each gap (never three: three is psytrance), and a synth arpeggio that layers up over minutes.

prog_b.name: Progressive House · arp build
prog_b.hint: A 16th-note arpeggio over an off-beat bass: the layer that keeps building across the track.

indie.name: Indie Dance
indie.hint: Straight kick, snare on 2 and 4, eighth hats, and a chunky synth bass riff that carries the song.

indie_b.name: Indie Dance · Tel Aviv, 122
indie_b.hint: Driving 16th hats, a bass riff with attitude and an acid line: the Maccabi House side.

indie_c.name: Indie Dance · Indie Tech, 125
indie_c.hint: Tech-house punch with a bold synth hook on top: a hard clap, 16th hats, a bass that drives on the off-beats and a riff you can sing. The hook, not the drums, is what makes it Indie.

disco.name: Disco
disco.hint: A live band, not a loop: hats on every 16th that open on the off-beat, soft ghost snares, a busy octave bass that jumps ahead of the beat, choppy 16th guitar and strings. House keeps the kick and drops the band.

nudisco.name: Nu Disco
nudisco.hint: Straight kick, open hats on the off-beat, and a funky octave-jumping disco bassline with chord stabs.

nudisco_b.name: Nu Disco · French touch
nudisco_b.hint: A filtered disco loop: pumping chord stabs on every off-beat and a bouncing bass.

techno.name: Techno
techno.hint: A long, hard kick with a ghost kick just before beats 2 and 4, a fast 16th hat over the off-beat hat, and a rumble under the kick instead of a bass hook.

techno_melodic.name: Techno · melodic, 124
techno_melodic.hint: Afterlife-style: a techno kick under a dark minor sequence. The bass runs in 16ths but changes note and plays across the kick: it is a melody, not psytrance's kick-bass-bass-bass.

techno_dub.name: Techno · dub techno, 124
techno_dub.hint: One minor chord, hit on syncopated 16ths and left to echo; an off-beat hat, a soft clap on 2 and 4, and a two-note sub. The chord never changes: that is the difference from deep house.

psy.name: Psytrance · rolling bass, 140
psy.hint: A short kick on every beat and the bass on the three 16ths in between, the first one softer: kick-bass-bass-bass. Clap on 2 and 4, open hat on the off-beat.

psy_b.name: Psytrance · full-on, 145
psy_b.hint: The same kick-bass-bass-bass machine, faster and busier, with more acid on top.

psy_c.name: Psytrance · progressive, off-beat bass, 132
psy_c.hint: Progressive psy: one bass note an 8th after each kick, as long as an 8th. Even at 126-132 this is Psytrance when the psy FX are there.

bass.name: Bass
bass.hint: Halftime: kick on 1, ONE snare on 3, syncopated hats and shaker that stop for the snare, and a held sub that is the main event. 140 that feels like 70.

bass_b.name: Bass · psydub
bass_b.hint: Halftime with dub space: one snare on 3, rim echoes, a deep moving sub and a psychedelic squelch.

bass_c.name: Bass · halftime, 170
bass_c.hint: DnB speed, halftime weight: the snare lands once per bar while the hats keep running at 170. Feels like 85.

dnb.name: DnB (drum and bass)
dnb.hint: Full-speed breakbeat: kick on 1 and the 'and' of 3, snares on 2 and 4, busy hats. Fast, never halftime.

dnb_b.name: DnB · liquid
dnb_b.hint: The same fast break, softer: rolling hats, a warm sub and chords floating over it.

dnb_c.name: DnB · jungle (Amen), 165
dnb_c.hint: The chopped Amen break: snares that stumble in late, kicks that come early, a ride on the off-beats, and a deep reggae sub under it.

salsa.name: Salsa · son clave 3-2
salsa.hint: The clave plays three hits in bar 1 and two in bar 2, and everything else bends around it: a slap on 2 and two open tones on 4 in the congas, a bass that lands before the beat, and a bell.

cumbia.name: Cumbia · scraper and drums (sketch)
cumbia.hint: No house kick: a low drum on 1 and 3, a small drum calling on 2 and 4, a scraper shuffling on the off-beats and a bass that moves root to fifth.

reggaeton.name: Reggaeton · dembow
reggaeton.hint: The dembow: a kick on every beat and the snare on the 'and-a' (boom-ch-boom-chick). This beat, not the language, makes it Reggaeton.

moombahton.name: Reggaeton · moombahton
moombahton.hint: Reggaeton's dembow snare over a house kick, slowed to about 108, with Dutch-house synth stabs. The snare on the 3+3+2 is what sets it apart from slow house: slow house keeps its snare or clap on 2 and 4.

dembow_do.name: Reggaeton · Dominican dembow
dembow_do.hint: The same boom-ch-boom-chick, pushed to about 115–130 and played hard: a kick on every beat, claps on 2 and 4, busy hats and a cowbell.

arrocha.name: Arrocha
arrocha.hint: A bolero for the dance floor: a soft kick on 1 and 3, clap on 2 and 4, keyboard chords answering on every off-beat, a bass on root and fifth, and a sax between the vocal lines.

sertanejo.name: Sertanejo · vanera (batidão), 90 (sketch)
sertanejo.hint: A live kit in 2/4: a kick on every beat, the snare on the last 16th of beat 1 and the 'and' of beat 2, eighth hats, and an acoustic guitar strum with muted slaps on the snare spots. An accordion leads. The snare cell is the same one reggaeton uses: the accordion, the guitar and the Portuguese vocal tell them apart. Kit and strum follow a published transcription; the bass and the accordion line are only illustrations.

sertanejo_raiz.name: Sertanejo · pagode de viola, 108 (sketch)
sertanejo_raiz.hint: No drums: a ten-string viola and a guitar, in 2/4. The guitar rests, then strikes two quick chords on the off-beat, over and over, with a muted stroke on each beat. The viola picks quick notes over the top. The strum follows published transcriptions; the viola line is only approximate.

funk.name: Brazilian Funk · tamborzão
funk.hint: No snare on 2 and 4: a big kick, low drums and hand-drum slaps play 'tum pa-pá pum pá' over and over. The MC raps on top of that drum line.

funk150.name: Brazilian Funk · funk 150
funk150.hint: The same 'tum pa-pá pum pá', pushed to 150 at the Baile da Gaiola, with an extra kick before the last slap and a long 808 underneath.

funk_volt.name: Brazilian Funk · Volt Mix (1990s)
funk_volt.hint: The older Miami-bass base: a dry 808 with a snare on 2 and 4, eighth hats, a few off-beat kicks and four electric clicks at the top of the bar.

bregafunk.name: Brega Funk
bregafunk.hint: Fast but felt at half speed: one clap per bar, a wobbly kick, a triangle-like clink on the off-beats, a bass that jumps up and down an octave, and a bright keyboard riff. Pitched snares climb into each turn.

axe_sambareggae.name: Axé · samba-reggae surdos, 104
axe_sambareggae.hint: Massed bass drums (surdos): the higher one lands on beats 1 and 3, the lower one on 2 and 4, and the small 'dobra' surdo rolls 16ths into the next beat. A repique (a high two-stick drum) chatters on the off-beats and the snares play a reggae-style backbeat. No kick drum.

axe.name: Axé · carnival band (sketch)
axe.hint: A band over Bahian drums: surdos mark every beat (higher on 1 and 3, lower on 2 and 4), the snare backs 2 and 4, the repique chatters, muted guitar chops sit on the off-beats and a horn stab punches. Bar 2 moves from Am to F and G.

pagodao.name: Pagodão · swingueira groove (sketch)
pagodao.hint: Hand drums lead, not a drum kit. A low surdo (big bass drum) thumps on beats 2 and 4 and a higher one answers on 1 and 3, a tall timbau and a small repique play the off-beat accents, a pandeiro (tambourine) runs 16ths, and a cavaquinho chops chords on the off-beats over a plain bass. Bar 2 ends with a repique roll into the loop.

samba.name: Samba · batucada (sketch)
samba.hint: A marching drum line: a deep surdo marks beats 2 and 4, a higher one answers on 1 and 3, the caixa runs 16ths, the tamborim plays its short figure and the bells keep time.

reggae.name: Reggae · one drop
reggae.hint: The one drop: kick and rim together on beat 3, nothing on beat 1, the skank on every off-beat, and a melodic bass.

reggae_steppers.name: Reggae · steppers (dub)
reggae_steppers.hint: The one drop with the kick on every beat: still only one rim, on beat 3, the skank on the off-beats and echo on everything. Compare its slow 4/4 with Organic House's.

hiphop.name: Hip Hop · boom bap
hiphop.hint: Boom-bap: kick on 1 and off the beat, snare on 2 and 4, swung hats, a sampled keys loop. The rapper carries the rest.

trap.name: Trap
trap.hint: Halftime: clap on beat 3, gaps in the kick, fast rolling hats, and a long 808 that slides. Compare its hats with Bass.

futurebass.name: Trap · future bass
futurebass.hint: Halftime like trap, but the chords lead: bright, wide chords that duck on every kick, with the clap on beat 3.

rock.name: Rock
rock.hint: A live kit: kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, eighth hats, a bass driving straight eighths and distorted power chords. Bar 2 ends with a snare-and-tom fill into the crash.

country.name: Country · boom-chick, 110
country.hint: The two-beat: a kick on 1 and 3, a light brushed snare on 2 and 4, a bass that alternates root and fifth, and a guitar chord answering on 2 and 4. A fiddle (played here by a lead synth) sings the tune over it. Bar 2 moves from G to C and D.

country_train.name: Country · train beat, 120 (sketch)
country_train.hint: The train beat, heard on the classic outlaw-country records: the snare never stops, a run of quiet 16ths with two loud hits on 2 and 4, over a kick on 1 and 3 and a boom-chick-a guitar. Sources disagree on where the loud hits fall; this draws them on 2 and 4.
